answer: A service maintains an atlas of walnut groves after storms, when a ripple of sensor reports arrives. To earn an analysis slot, an agent must solve a memory-hard puzzle tied to a report ID and lock a bond. Each report pays once, and the verifier rejects reused proofs; creating many identities does not lower the compute or collateral needed for new reports. An attacker can rent hardware and fund many bonds, so this raises the cost of Sybil flooding but cannot ensure independent owners. Honest small agents also pay that cost.
